General_Description.Text: FOCM is an ultrafast optical clearing method designed to rapidly clarify tissue slices with minimal tissue deformation and fluorescence quenching. It uses a combination of dehydration with water-miscible polar solvent and hydration with urea, along with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), D-sorbitol, and glycerol. This method can clear 300-μm-thick brain slices within 2 minutes, maintain fluorescence signals up to 86% after 11 days, and control tissue linear expansion to only a 2.12% increase. FOCM is compatible with various labeling methods and improves imaging depth and quality, making it suitable for high-throughput analysis and emergent clinical diagnosis.
Text_Reference: Here, we developed an ultrafast optical clearing method (FOCM) with simple protocols and common reagents to overcome these limitations.
The results show that FOCM can rapidly clarify 300-μm-thick brain slices within 2 min.
By using FOCM, we successfully built the detailed 3D nerve cells model and showed the connection between neuron, astrocyte, and blood vessel.
FOCM Combines Dehydration of Solvent with Hyperhydration, Enabling an Ultrafast Tissue Clearing with Negligible Distortion.
Considering the clearing efficiency, we used DMSO as a solvent for its features of low toxicity, high dissolving ability, and protein partially denatured capacity.
Notably, with the utilization of urea, 300-μm-thick fragile brain slices became much firmer and could be easily handled.
To examine the clearing capacity, we implemented FOCM to 300-μm-thick brain slices, brain hemisphere, and internal organs, respectively.

Compared with CLARITY and CUBIC, which aim to achieve a very efficient clearing results of whole organ/body with delipidation, FOCM aims at ultrafast tissue slices clearing with high fluorescent preservation and simple protocol.
The results show that 86% of GFP fluorescent signals by FOCM could be preserved after 11 d.

Besides, there was only 2.12% tissue expansion after FOCM treatment compared with 22.0% expansion with CLARITY, 15.9% expansion with CUBIC, 24.5% expansion with ScaleS, and 13.5% shrinkage with SeeDB.
To investigate the relationship between tissue expansion or shrinkage with cell morphology distortion, we merged the images of soma with dendrites before and after clearing.
The possible reason might be tissue expansion or shrinkage and the unavoidable human-made distortion during multisteps treatment in CLARITY, CUBIC, ScaleS, and SeeDB.
The results show that all of the methods preserved the morphology of soma as in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), but only FOCM could merge the dendrites before and after clearing.
The above results show that FOCM can improve imaging depth nearly three times in LSCM with SBR increasing average 38.2 at the depth of 80 μm and deeper.
Therefore, FOCM has the potential to be a widely used sample mounting media for biological optical imaging.

Text1_Reference: Optical clearing is a versatile approach to improve imaging quality and depth of optical microscopy by reducing scattered light. However, conventional optical clearing methods are restricted in the efficiency-first applications due to unsatisfied time consumption, irreversible tissue deformation, and fluorescence quenching. Here, we developed an ultrafast optical clearing method (FOCM) with simple protocols and common reagents to overcome these limitations. The results show that FOCM can rapidly clarify 300-μm-thick brain slices within 2 min.
